profile.summary: BulkRNABert is a transformer language model for bulk RNA-seq data. It takes the expression levels of a fixed set of genes from one sample and returns embeddings of that sample. The embeddings are used to build downstream models for cancer-type classification and survival-time prediction.
profile.summary_source_locator: PMLR abstract; README.md: 1. BulkRNABert; model card: introduction

summary_quotes.text: we develop a pre-trained transformer-based language model through self-supervised learning using bulk RNA-seq from both non-cancer and cancer tissues, following BERT’s masking method
we then build downstream models for cancer-type classification and survival-time prediction

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: BulkRNABert is an encoder-only transformer. Each gene in the input is one token, and its expression value is binned and embedded together with a gene embedding. During pretraining, expression values are masked at random and the model learns to reconstruct them from the other genes, as in BERT. The released configuration has 4 transformer layers, an embedding size of 256, 8 attention heads, 64 expression bins and 19,062 genes. For a downstream task the authors either probe the learned embeddings or use parameter-efficient fine-tuning.

quotes.text: BulkRNABert is a transformer-based, encoder-only language model pre-trained on bulk RNA-seq profiles from the TCGA dataset using self-supervised masked language modeling, following the original BERT framework.
The model is trained to reconstruct randomly masked gene expression values from their genomic context
By probing learned embeddings from the model or using parameter-efficient fine-tuning

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The repository ships three pretrained checkpoints in JAX: bulk_rna_bert_tcga (pretrained on TCGA), bulk_rna_bert_gtex_encode (GTEx and ENCODE) and bulk_rna_bert_gtex_encode_tcga (a mix of all three). It also ships a classification model for five TCGA cohorts used in an example notebook. The Hugging Face repository InstaDeepAI/BulkRNABert holds a PyTorch version for the transformers library, described as pretrained on TCGA, plus the JAX parameters. A result should name the checkpoint, the framework and the commit or Hugging Face revision; this page read the repository at commit bfdc2ab8 and the Hugging Face card at revision 4ee84d56.
sections.source_locator: README.md: 1. BulkRNABert, Downstream task example; model card: Other notes

quotes.text: **bulk_rna_bert_gtex_encode**: BulkRNABert pre-trained on GTEx and ENCODE data
**bulk_rna_bert_gtex_encode_tcga**: BulkRNABert pre-trained on a mix of GTEx, ENCODE and TCGA data.
An example notebook `examples/downstream_task_example.ipynb` illustrates an inference with the classification model trained on the 5 cohorts (BRCA, BLCA, GBMLGG, LUAD, UCEC) classification problem.
We also provide the params for the BulkRNABert jax model in `jax_params`.

sections.title: Input preparation
sections.body: The model expects expression values for a fixed list of genes, given in common_gene_id.txt, in a fixed order. The repository includes a script that turns raw RNA-seq files downloaded from the GDC portal into this format, using the unstranded TPM column in its example. The Hugging Face example applies log10(1 + x) to the expression values before tokenising and checks that the number of columns equals the model's gene count.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Transcriptomic language model: an encoder-only transformer pretrained with masked language modelling on bulk RNA-seq profiles.

quotes.text: BulkRNABert is a transformer-based, encoder-only language model pre-trained on bulk RNA-seq profiles

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Transformer encoder with 4 layers, embedding size 256, 8 attention heads (key size 32) and feed-forward size 512. Each gene is a token; expression values are discretised into 64 bins, and gene embeddings are used.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A bulk RNA-seq gene expression profile over the model's fixed list of genes, in the order given by common_gene_id.txt. The repository's preprocessing example uses TPM values from GDC files.

quotes.text: a text file `common_gene_id.txt` that indicates the gene ids that must be used (and in which order they should appear)

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Per-gene embeddings from chosen transformer layers, averaged in the examples to one embedding per sample. Downstream models built on the embeddings give cancer-type classification and survival predictions.
facts.source_locator: README.md: 1. BulkRNABert inference snippet; model card: Other notes

quotes.text: embeddings can be used for downstream tasks.

facts.value: Bulk RNA-seq from cancer and non-cancer tissues. The three released checkpoints were pretrained on TCGA, on GTEx and ENCODE, and on a mix of GTEx, ENCODE and TCGA. TCGA data were obtained through the GDC portal.

run_guide.summary: Install the repository package at a pinned commit and compute BulkRNABert embeddings for the bundled TCGA sample with the bulk_rna_bert_tcga checkpoint.
prerequisites: Python 3.10 or later, as setup.py requires.
The package pins jax==0.4.19, jaxlib==0.4.19 and dm-haiku==0.0.10. GPU type and memory are not stated in the sources read.
Code and weights are Apache-2.0; the sample TCGA data stay under their source's terms.

steps.title: Compute embeddings for the sample data
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import haiku as hk
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
import pandas as pd

from multiomics_open_research.bulk_rna_bert.pretrained import get_bulkrnabert_pretrained_model
from multiomics_open_research.common.preprocess import preprocess_omic

# Get pretrained model
parameters, forward_fn, tokenizer, config = get_bulkrnabert_pretrained_model(
    model_name="bulk_rna_bert_tcga",
    embeddings_layers_to_save=(4,),
    checkpoint_directory="checkpoints/",
)
forward_fn = hk.transform(forward_fn)

# Get bulk RNASeq data and tokenize it
gene_expression_df = pd.read_csv("data/bulkrnabert/tcga_sample.csv")
gene_expression_array = preprocess_omic(gene_expression_df, config)
gene_expression_ids = tokenizer.batch_tokenize(gene_expression_array)
gene_expression_ids = jnp.asarray(gene_expression_ids, dtype=jnp.int32)

# Inference
random_key = jax.random.PRNGKey(0)
outs = forward_fn.apply(parameters, random_key, gene_expression_ids)

# Get mean embeddings from layer 4
gene_expression_mean_embeddings = outs["embeddings_4"].mean(axis=1)
PY
steps.explanation: The README inference snippet, wrapped in a shell heredoc and run from the repository root. Replace bulk_rna_bert_tcga with bulk_rna_bert_gtex_encode or bulk_rna_bert_gtex_encode_tcga to use the other checkpoints.

quotes.text: parameters, forward_fn, tokenizer, config = get_bulkrnabert_pretrained_model( model_name="bulk_rna_bert_tcga", embeddings_layers_to_save=(4,), checkpoint_directory="checkpoints/", )

outputs: An array of mean layer-4 embeddings, one row per sample in tcga_sample.csv, held in memory. The snippet prints nothing and writes no file.

Own data must first be converted to the model's gene list, for example with scripts/preprocess_tcga_rna_seq.py for GDC files.
